lessons.rationale: The scan and cost-model caveat teach linear work directly. Exact setup arithmetic adds no insight, so no equation remains. The correctness question separates precise procedure, valid-input termination and correct outputs from efficiency.

Pair avoidance and no-duplicate worst case remain visible; the exact triangular count is useful budgeting reference only. All three questions test quadratic scaling, actual nested ranges and sorting/hash alternatives, with constant work explicitly assumed.

The scan/square/subset relationship earns one essential card because the objective is distinguishing these growth shapes. Doubling and candidate-check assumptions remain visible; questions predict eventual scaling and worst-case input doubling.

Uniform operation speedup, sufficient memory and constant candidate-check cost visibly delimit the hardware claims. Capacity gains are explained in words; the questions reason about square-root and additive gains without numeric substitutions.

Item count, independent graph dimensions, pixels and encoded bits are explained before dominant terms. No equation is needed; questions diagnose numeric-value versus bit-length cost, finite-size constants and doubled image dimensions.

The fixed multiplier/threshold definition is essential to this lesson. Visible prose explains universal large-size coverage and loose bounds; questions test proof obligations and the valid but loose linear upper bound for binary search.

Omega and Theta definitions remain essential to compare bounds. Sorted/reverse-sorted insertion cases and an alternating-size counterexample explain why the input case and tightness are separate. Questions reason across both input families.

Log-base conversion is optional reference; its complete constant-rescaling meaning stays visible. Dominance and exponential-base contrast are explained without substitution. Quiz formula data stay expanded and test dominant growth rather than coefficient arithmetic.

Ratio limits and the factorial-log sandwich argument are fully visible without equations. Quiz cards supply all compared functions, so ordering, limits and quasi-polynomial reasoning require interpretation rather than recalled formulas.

Sequential addition, independent dimensions and dependent triangular work are taught from executed ranges. Code is retained because control flow is the object of study. The print-count question states its I/O abstraction.

The three short code patterns expose distinct update/start behaviours. Visible geometric and threshold counting replaces summation calculations. Questions distinguish one-more update, linear geometric totals and linear summed doubling distances.
The step-size code and doubling-band explanation make the harmonic factor visible. No formal harmonic sum is needed; the standalone question now explicitly assumes constant work and arithmetic.

Fibonacci repeated subproblems and list membership/slicing are the mechanisms. Short code remains; questions test memoisation, representation choice and copies. End-pop amortised cost is explicitly separated from other worst-case operations.

The lesson states input distributions and fixed-input random-pivot assumptions in visible prose. Questions distinguish those probability models from input extremes and reject universal early-exit guarantees.

Peak-live space, input/output conventions, shared-object slots and atomic-value assumptions precede the examples. Code demonstrates eager versus lazy evaluation. Questions count retained storage without hidden byte calculations.

Live-depth versus total-call reasoning and integer-bit caveats remain visible. The cold-cache descent and CPython tail-call limitation are source-checked. Questions diagnose frames, cached descent and retained merge buffers under a standard array-sort convention.

Swapping code defines actual mutation/alias behaviour. Visible prose distinguishes mutation from strict constant auxiliary space and explains smaller-side recursion plus a loop. Questions test these invariants rather than calculating stack constants.

Visible trade-offs cover mutation permission, hash memory, sorted two-position scanning, update-sensitive prefixes and representation overhead. The80MB illustration is conditional and recomputed; questions choose methods from memory/output constraints.

The from-empty copy/write model and geometric spacing suffice to prove linear sequence cost; exact copy sums are unnecessary. Questions distinguish amortised guarantees from per-call latency and probabilistic averages.

The three-unit charge is explained through a nonnegative prefix balance with initial-capacity and append-only assumptions. No equation is needed. The question diagnoses spending credit before collecting it.

Actual cost plus potential change is essential because it defines the method. The specific array potential is reference-only; visible text preserves zero-capacity start, nonnegative potential and prefix bounds. Questions interpret releases and telescoping, with Phi defined locally.

The copy-on-resize model, fixed versus proportional growth and separated thresholds remain visible. Questions reason about frequency, thrashing and fixed factors; numeric growth examples are policy choices, not product guarantees.

Counter-flip frequency and one-transfer-per-item queue accounting are explained without sums. Visible limitations cover deadlines, real preallocation, chunk allocation and persistent version reuse. Questions diagnose lifetime work and the vector relocation slow path.

One essential comparison card connects one versus two children with constant versus linear outside work. Code and base-case/rounding assumptions remain visible. The question supplies constant-cost indexing/updates and tests actual executed branches.

The level-cost mechanisms and tree drawing teach equal, growing and shrinking level totals. Quiz scenarios name children and outside work, so classification follows explanation without arithmetic or a formula lookup.

The equal-fraction recurrence/critical exponent and fixed power-gap case remain essential definitions. Visible base-case and rounding conditions prevent mechanical misuse; questions reason about leaf growth and reducing recursive products.

The nonnegative-log-power extension remains essential, with a visible per-level argument and explicit excluded negative powers. Quiz cards supply recurrences; explanations trace level accumulation rather than exponent substitution.

The power-gap and regularity inequalities remain essential proof conditions. Visible half-cost levels explain the root-dominated result. The question provides its recurrence and tests why later levels add only a constant multiple.

The failed fixed-multiplier induction is essential to expose a proof error; mismatched recurrence forms are explained in prose. The repaired distractor now falsely claims the missing base case is the only issue, leaving one correct answer.

The balancing recurrence is essential; the integral is genuinely reference material. Fixed positive weights/fractions, bounded base costs, polynomial-growth condition and exact/rounded distinction stay visible. Unequal-child questions use shrinking-level reasoning with the integral closed.

Selection is explicitly an upper-bound recurrence with constant corrections. The log-gap recurrence/result is essential to identify the case omitted by the stated Master theorem; the visible harmonic-level argument supports the question without evaluating the optional integral.

Workload-specific counts/rates, input ceilings and memory boundaries replace invented universal throughput or exponential cutoffs. All questions diagnose missing evidence, bounded exhaustive search and invalid rate extrapolation.

Small-run caps, CPython3.14 sorting policy and row-major locality are explained as mechanisms with measured-performance limits. The C code is the question objective. No asymptotic exponent ratio is presented as a practical speedup.

Attacker-chosen collisions, backtracking and bad pivots are distinguished from fixed small workloads. Unsupported exact outage growth was replaced with directly reported excessive backtracking; the question still tests input-controlled amplification.

Doubling ratios are diagnostic evidence, not proofs; the supplied numbers test interpretation. Front-pop code explains observed growth, and stream top-k selection follows output/memory needs. Measurement/GC and mutation constraints remain visible.

No formulas needed. Retain the complete fetch component because per-setup flags, HTTP errors and guarded success/error branches are the mechanism under study. Three unchanged questions predict response ordering, distinguish HTTP failure from Promise rejection and select observable lifecycle checks; contract and cancellation limits remain visible.

No mathematical formulas needed; the increments are executable code illustrating local state, not a maths exercise. Retain both short Hook examples to show independent state and subscriptions. Rewrite q1 from arithmetic output to a prediction about which caller changes, explicitly stating local useState in the prompt. Unchanged q2/q3 test subscription ownership and useful Hook interfaces/cleanup.

No equations needed. Retain the small nested-provider example so nearest ancestry and fallback can be traced. All three unchanged questions predict provider values, explain memoised consumer updates and choose sensible context ownership; default/provider facts remain in visible prose.

No formulas or invented timings. Retain useMemo and useCallback snippets because dependency identity and functional updates are the mechanisms being contrasted. Three unchanged questions choose measurement, distinguish the caches and diagnose in-place mutation. No measured speedup or compiler execution is asserted.

No formulas needed. Retain the complete small app because composing state, filtering and immutable toggles is the objective. The three unchanged questions predict filtered-toggle results, choose minimal state and diagnose loss of removed row-local state; the behavioural checklist supplies direct evidence without extra analogies.

modules.subject: software-engineering
modules.title: Software Architecture at the Code Level

lessons.rationale: Frequency/period reciprocals stay in prose; their duplicate card was removed. Wavelength conversion remains a useful physical reference, with units and speed assumptions visible. The question predicts shorter periods without calculation.
Cycle position, radians and cancellation are explained by the table and prose without an equation card. Both questions test unit contracts and phase behaviour; every required conversion is visible.

The sine relationship is the sole essential card because interpreting how its parameters combine is the objective. Angular-frequency conversion is already explicit in prose, so its redundant card was removed. Quarter-cycle output tests parameter meaning.

The two reference cards support oscillator implementation: samples per cycle and phase advance in both units. Visible prose explains their inverse changes, non-integer periods and clock mismatch. All four questions test behaviour rather than substitution.

Wrapped state and preserved phase are the objective, so keep the two short runnable examples and remove glide derivations. The clock-hand analogy maps position versus speed with rounding/slope limits. Questions diagnose resets, numerical spacing and changing-frequency history.

Equal pitch intervals are ratios; doubling and midpoint examples establish the mechanism. Remove the redundant semitone card while retaining its numeric multiplier in prose. Questions compare pitch-space operations rather than recall logarithm identities.

Keep both reference conversions because note-to-frequency synthesis and frequency-to-note tuning need different directions. The compact mapping function and integer-division question teach an actual implementation trap. Tuning convention and display-label assumptions stay visible.

Two cents conversion references serve measuring and applying detune; the beat equation merely repeats frequency-difference prose and was removed. The tuner code makes nearest-note behaviour explicit. Questions predict signed detune and register-dependent beats. Unnecessary secondary hearing thresholds were removed.

Keep one reference card comparing fixed-hertz with fixed-cents control: it documents the implementation distinction. Visible prose supplies the ratio behaviour, pitch-space addition and one-volt-per-octave example. Questions choose consistent units and diagnose register-dependent modulation.

Harmonic order, amplitude recipe and missing fundamental are complete in prose without cards. Questions interpret a supplied close-frequency pair and missing fundamental. Corrected mixing feedback: addition creates no new spectral frequencies but existing components can beat.

Two reference cards support actual callback deadline and memory/data budgeting. Main prose gives the scaling, sample-time meaning and hardware-slot caveat. Questions predict resource changes, keeping arithmetic optional.

The step-size and nearest-rounding bound remain one reference for quantiser design; visible prose and the ruler analogy explain both. Retain the short quantiser trace because rounding versus endpoint saturation is the code objective. All keys match executed code.

Keep the useful SQNR estimate as reference with uniform-error and overload assumptions visible. Executed code tests those assumptions at coarse resolution; removing derivations preserves the failure mechanism. Questions distinguish six-dB-per-bit behaviour, overload and signal level.

No equation is necessary: dither trades noise for removal of correlated error, while measured analogue noise limits converter performance. Questions test this and separate word length, dynamic range and SINAD. Added noiseless nearest-rounding assumptions to the sub-step question.

No cards: the short conversion program demonstrates scaling, rounding and clamping. Question checks float headroom, precision and format boundaries. Corrected feedback so float storage does not promise that every intermediate effect avoids clipping.

Nyquist is explained as a strict boundary and sample ambiguity; no duplicate inequality card remains. The executed sign-inverted-sine example demonstrates the ambiguity. Questions predict rate changes and distinguish ideal reconstruction from plots and aliases.

The wrap/reflection algorithm remains a useful general reference because several sample-rate intervals are possible. The matching short code is the operational objective. Questions trace direction and irrecoverability; phase caveats remain visible.

Infinite harmonic tails, jumps and alias locations are explained in prose with an executed prediction table. No repeated harmonic or phase equations are needed. Questions diagnose inharmonic folds; clarified that some higher folds coincide with genuine harmonic bins.

No notation is needed to compare prevention before sampling, band-limited generation and filtered oversampling. Questions identify sources and supplied folds. Clarified that a genuine harmonic bin can also contain higher folded contributions.

No equation is needed because the explicit image-frequency example and sequential conversion chain explain the distinction. The question chooses the supplied out-of-band images; reconstruction cannot remove an already folded in-band alias.

Three reference cards are justified as distinct practical conversions: power ratio, amplitude ratio and dB back to gain. Their factors and unchanged-impedance condition stay visible. Questions interpret gain and serial composition rather than compute logarithms.

Three references support actual measurement: dBFS, RMS recipe and crest factor. Visible prose supplies signs, waveform differences, meter conventions and true-peak caveat. Questions distinguish peak from average level without computing a sum.

Remove the voice-scaling card because both policies are already completely specified in prose. Executed summing experiment demonstrates peak risk beyond average power. Refined analogy to simultaneous drain flow and retained signed-value/statistical limits. Questions compare coherent peaks, power and design choices.

No transfer equations are needed: prose states clamping and tanh behaviour. The compact measured comparison is the objective. Question feedback now qualifies represented-band audibility and ties the ninth-harmonic comparison to the demonstrated drive.

No cards: the signal-flow checklist teaches headroom placement. Clarified intermediate effect limits and finite rounding rather than promising that float pipelines never clip. Questions diagnose measured peak versus RMS and the normal final conversion boundary.

Keep one voltage conversion reference for dBu/dBV application; nominal versus maximum, device matching and electrical/hearing precautions stay visible. The question selects safe matching checks rather than RMS-to-peak arithmetic.

Keep the three executable diagnostics because measuring real arrays is the objective; remove the duplicate zero-crossing equation. Whole-cycle/DC limitations and hearing precautions remain visible. Questions map bugs to suitable measurements rather than substitute values.

Keep one grouped FFT reference for array length, spacing and bin centres. Added visible real-spectrum symmetry, odd/even endpoint distinction and the frequency-axis API prerequisite. Questions choose observation length, axis construction and actual resolution versus padding.

Keep one reference amplitude-normalisation card because code must compensate the actual window sum and endpoint exceptions. Execute the compact measurement function. Question diagnoses scaling while all prerequisites remain visible.

No cards: the executed comparison and concrete readings explain leakage and scalloping. Questions choose a window or amplitude method and retain the resolution trade-off; removed feedback arithmetic and universal claims about exact FFTs or always-worthwhile widening.

Unchanged after full semantic review: compact spectrum code tests predicted folds and coincident aliases directly. No formula cards. The question interprets a supplied 3 kHz square-wave spectrum and its harmonic-level discrepancy rather than requiring a derivation.

No cards: export/readback is the code objective. Executed rate, subtype and error checks with PCM and float boundary experiments. Clarified default float64 reads can exceed nominal full scale for FLOAT files and float32 export can round.

No equation is needed to choose a synthesis approach. The method table, subtractive/additive mechanisms, Fourier midpoint qualification and hedged memory/CPU trade-offs were checked against the Moog Model D manual and JOS additive synthesis; q11 now diagnoses the design choice without DC arithmetic.

The sideband-spacing relation is useful reference maths; its visible In words line and the 400/100 Hz example carry the idea. PM/FM equivalence, DC-offset behaviour, index distribution, Chowning 1967 and DX7 1983 checked against JOS and Yamaha; q2 tests construction recognition.

The Karplus-Strong delay-length division was removed; the loop-period idea and 218/109-sample examples (48 kHz) stay in prose with filter delay and fractional delay qualified. History claims checked against BYTE 1977, JOS taxonomy, PPG and Waldorf pages. 'Round trip' reworded to 'loop' because it opened a networking definition.

Block diagram and audio/control distinction need no maths. Lesson text unchanged except that control-signal update caveat is retained; q6 feedback had a stale 'lesson 7' pointer, now pointing to the control-rate unit.

Executable note-stack sketch is the learning objective; output 60 64 60 None re-run and matched. Zero-velocity note-on as note-off checked against MIDI Association sources. Files unchanged since the previous stamp; questions q4/q7 already test traces and diagnosis.

Allocator sketch retained because its behaviour is the objective (re-run: [0, 1, 0]). Paraphony qualified against the Matriarch manual; q8 now asks for target-board budgeting instead of percentage arithmetic; chair analogy mapping and limit checked.

inc = f/f_s is the one essential relationship for the module and stays visible; the duplicate waveform formula card was removed in favour of the short Python shape functions (values at phase 0.25 recomputed: 1, -0.5, 0). q1 tests prediction of doubling the increment.

The block-rate division card was removed; the persistent-phase code was re-run (0.666667; 0.9239 0.866) and the 750 Hz block-repetition warning recomputed. q2 keeps the reset diagnosis (1 kHz repetition at 48-sample blocks).

MIDI-to-frequency is useful but not needed for the concept, so it is a reference card with a standalone In words line; note 60 = 261.63 Hz and note 81 = 880 Hz recomputed. The single question was already conceptual and unchanged.

p - floor(p) is kept essential because the wrap rule is the objective; cents-arithmetic removed. Reset-to-zero code re-run (44.0 / 1090.9 Hz vs 1100 Hz, about 14.4 cents flat); C fmod sign behaviour checked in C11 N1570. Running-track analogy mapping/limit checked.

The DDS increment/wrap/index relations are reference maths; increment 89,478,485 and 0.000011 Hz resolution recomputed. PJRC uint32_t accumulator checked in pinned source. q7 now tests the role of low phase bits. A dangling colon left by the removed resolution card was fixed.

Spacing/rounding derivation cards removed; the float32 experiment was re-run (439.5, 445.3, 468.8, 375.0 Hz) and the wrapped-accumulator claim recomputed (439.99972 Hz, about -0.001 cents). 2^24 counter limit (about 5.8 min) and float32 spacing checked against NumPy finfo. q8-q10 test diagnosis.

No maths needed. DaisySP Reset/SetFreq and PJRC phase/frequency interfaces checked in the pinned sources. q11 hedging from the earlier incomplete pass was reviewed and accepted: free-running phase can vary but can recur; reset alone does not guarantee an identical attack.

The series formula was removed; the visible prose keeps DC, harmonic grid, phase and midpoint convergence. Overtone wording was aligned with the newly verified synth/01 overtone entry (fundamental is not an overtone). q1 tests the 10 ms -> 100 Hz grid without calculation.

Three series cards and the dB conversion card were removed; fundamental amplitudes 0.637/1.273/0.811 and -6, -9.5, -19, -28 dB levels recomputed. A sentence pointing to a removed code example was rewritten. q1-q3 now test spectral predictions.
|sin(pi n w)|/n is a useful reference card with a standalone In words line; the visible rule (harmonic vanishes when n w is whole) supports q5, which supplies that rule. sin(pi/3) = 0.87 recomputed.

Bin spacing and amplitude normalisation stay as reference cards; DC/Nyquist exception checked against NumPy FFT docs. FFT code re-run (relative harmonics match; spacing tidied as stated). q4/q6/q7 now test predictions about length, normalisation and harmonic count.

The decibel derivation was removed; sine/cosine-phase code re-run (peaks 1.81 vs 4.25, 7.4 dB). Perceptual claim hedged to what Drennan et al. (Schroeder-phase discrimination) supports; Further-reading label fixed. Pushing analogy mapping/limit checked.

Gibbs constant card removed; 8.95 % of the jump, peak 1.179 and 1.43 dB recomputed and checked against NIST DLMF 6.16. The ambiguous '18% peak' was clarified as 18 % above the flat level. q10 tests the headroom response.

Folding relation kept as one reference card; alias table recomputed (23,100, 9,405, 690, 555 Hz; -26.0 to -31.8 dB). Aliasing wording verified as scoped to this example. q1 had a stale 'Lesson 3' pointer; q2/q3/q5 test combination, inharmonicity and folding direction.

Harmonic-limit ceiling rule retained as reference (19 harmonics at 1245 Hz, 479 at 50 Hz recomputed). Table range reasoning visible. q8 wording 'Precomputed tables' opened a password-cracking definition and was reworded; analogy 'spare capacity' likewise. Packing analogy checked.

No formula needed. Oversampling/decimation, BLIT (Stilson and Smith 1996), minBLEP (Brandt 2001) and PolyBLEP (Valimaki and Huovilainen 2007) attributions checked. q7/q12 qualifications from the earlier incomplete pass reviewed and accepted.

Polynomial substitution card removed; the PolyBLEP experiment was re-run (naive 9405 Hz -29.8 dB; PolyBLEP -55.4 dB; -1.9 dB at h10, -7.6 dB at h19) and compared with the DaisySP polynomial. Finke reading-list label fixed. q6/q10 test mechanism and trade-off.

Correction/DC formulas removed; pulse fragment executed in a harness at widths 0.5 and 0.3 (-55.45 dB corrected; naive -29.83 and -28.70 dB; mean -0.4). DaisySP numbers reproduced by a float32 port of the pinned source; PJRC 2*SUPPORT = 32-sample BLEP window read from source. q9 tests edge signs.
Linear-step formula removed; ADSR definitions and linear-fade perception remain visible. q1 now asks for a sound-design choice (lower sustain) instead of label recall.

The one-pole update/coefficient pair is reference maths; 63.2 %, 46.1 ms, 69.1 ms and 1e-5 = -100 dB recomputed and checked against JOS time-constant page. q2/q4/q9 test curve shape, relative thresholds and control contracts. Half-the-gap analogy checked; dangling colon fixed.
Duration derivation cards removed; the state machine was re-run (8.98 ms, 0.6, 2200 ms) and both durations recomputed from logarithmic ratios. q7 tests why the attack overshoots its target.

No maths needed. Phase-reset and log-domain glide wording from the earlier incomplete pass was checked and accepted (reset at matching values need not step; only a linear log-domain ramp gives equal time per interval). A reference to 'the code above' that lives in another unit was fixed.

Smoother cards removed; the one-pole/linear-ramp code re-run (0.632 0.865; 1.0 1.0). JUCE SmoothedValue behaviour checked. q3 qualifications (aliases persist, 128 CC values) from the earlier pass reviewed and accepted; q6 tests within-block steps.

The octave-share card was removed; 1 % vs 50.5 % shares recomputed. The cutoff bullet still implied octave-domain smoothing gives equal time per octave; it now states that only a constant-rate octave ramp does. Staircase analogy checked; q10 tests ramp-domain choice.
The octave-count card was removed; the qualified 6 dB/octave-per-pole asymptotic rule and order table remain visible. q1/q5 test asymptote use rather than arithmetic. Dangling colon fixed.
Gain-equals-Q card removed; RBJ low-pass gain at f0 recomputed (-3.01, +6.02, +12.04, +20.0 dB at 48 kHz/1 kHz) against the W3C cookbook. q6 tests headroom consequence of resonance.

The recurrence is essential and stays visible; the exp coefficient mapping is reference (EarLevel). State-per-voice explanation retained; moving-average analogy mapping/limit checked. q2/q4 test state ownership and step-response shape.

|H| is reference maths; measurement code re-run (0, -3.0, -12.2, -22.5 dB) and table/half-power points (1001.43, 5188.89, 11895 Hz; none for 15 kHz) recomputed. q9 stability explanation from the earlier pass reviewed and accepted.

Impulse-response and FIR sum cards removed; IIR/FIR table and BIBO/linear-phase statements checked against JOS. 'Recursive' wording opened the core recursion (function-call) definition and was changed to 'feedback'. q7 unchanged and correct.
|1 - a| < 1 kept essential because the stability condition is the objective; shortcut-coefficient limit fs/pi = 15.28 kHz recomputed. q8 tests the failure diagnosis.

Biquad difference equation is reference. Wishnick DAFx 2014 (DF-II transient/click, SVF time-varying stability proof) and Simper audio-rate statement checked; Chamberlin SVF stability bound recomputed (6.5-8.3 kHz at 48 kHz for Q 0.5-0.707). 'State structure' opened a React definition and was reworded.
Feedback and DC-gain cards removed; k = 4 marginal threshold and -12.04 dB at k = 3 checked against Stilson and Smith. Octave cutoff rule kept as prose. q10 tests the bass-loss mechanism.
Unipolar mapping and increment cards removed; LFO code re-run (0.0033333333333333335; 0.5 1.0). q1 tests mapping; q12 smoothing walkthrough from the earlier pass reviewed and accepted.

Tempo formula kept as reference (120 BPM quarter = 2 Hz). The duplicate tremolo gain card was removed. 'Free-running LFOs drift' was hedged to timing-dependent phase. q3/q10 test division and gain endpoints.

Cents conversion kept as reference; 427.47-452.89 and 415.30-466.16 Hz recomputed; q5 values (2.35 semitones, 7.9 cents) recomputed. A sentence was added so the linear-FM takeaway is supported in the body.

Octave-sum and conversion cards removed; matrix code re-run (1.787 octaves, 1726.0 Hz; 433.69 Hz). Overflow caveat from the earlier pass accepted. MIDI channel/poly-pressure statements checked. Thermostat analogy checked; q6/q8 test combination and voice ownership.

Block-rate and sideband cards removed; 1.5 kHz, 0.67 ms, about 1.5 steps per 1 ms attack and 300 updates per 5 Hz cycle recomputed. q11 pointer to 'the lesson's code' now names the LFO unit; q7 tests coarse attack steps.
Mean-frequency integral removed; 494.46 Hz (I0(ln 2)) and 440.37 Hz at +/-1 semitone recomputed. q9 tests why the arithmetic mean rises.
Measurable per-path requirements need no equation. Questions assess the observable goal, analytics cache policy and dependency choices; required HTTP facts stay visible.

Team, deadline, workload and constraints are direct decision inputs. No formulas are needed; retained classification questions distinguish targets from constraints, while the MVP question now requires benchmarking rather than arithmetic.

The cache-loss load example earns its short numeric result because it reveals a failure path. Removed substitutions add no insight; seat-inventory and admission questions reason from visible atomicity and capacity facts.

The transfer relationship is useful optional reference for separating propagation and transmission. Its visible reading and the 150 ms example suffice; all three questions select a remedy for a measured bottleneck, with capacity assumptions clarified.

The M/M/1 equation is reference, with assumptions and the qualitative saturation curve visible. Little-law arithmetic is deferred to its focused unit; questions identify waiting and survivor headroom without substituting into hidden formulas.

No equation is needed to explain a sorted percentile. The small distribution and explicit nearest-rank convention remain visible. Questions diagnose misleading averages, aggregation and omitted waiting; no arithmetic recall is necessary.

The independent-tail probability is one useful reference relationship, not a required derivation. The visible slowest-shard mechanism answers the questions. Hedging feedback now distinguishes additional requests from resource work and removes a guaranteed new tail.

The hypothetical timing table illustrates scale and access patterns without serving as a benchmark. No ratio formula is needed. The multi-answer question checks units and measurement; the lorry comparison has explicit delivery and handling limits.

One optional downtime relationship supports applying an SLO later. Visible time-versus-request definitions and nines comparisons answer the questions; reliability and durability remain separate. Recomputed downtime and corrected the 100-ms-per-minute percentage.

One parallel-availability reference card earns its place for independent alternatives. Survivor-capacity and switching assumptions remain visible; the two-of-three example gives its implication without combinatorial derivation. Questions diagnose success states and shared failures.

One optional series card supports later modelling. Its visible In words now includes independence; prose distinguishes required tiers from alternatives. Questions trace dependencies instead of multiplying percentages.

One optional renewal-cycle relationship helps compare failure frequency and recovery duration. Visible stages and levers answer both questions; redundant recovery arithmetic and its orphaned introduction are removed.

No equation is needed for scale-up versus scale-out and hidden state. Questions follow sessions, rate counters and replaceable instances; local-memory behaviour is explained directly. Token wording avoids the unrelated certificate dictionary sense.

Amdahl is retained as a single optional fixed-job reference; the serial-floor explanation and limits remain visible. Pair counts give intuition without a second formula; removed dangling equation references. Questions diagnose shared-resource and coordination limits.

One Little-law card is useful reference for sizing a resource held over time. The three occupancy examples show the slow-dependency mechanism. Questions distinguish average occupancy from capacity and explain thread exhaustion rather than compute it.

Unit tables and explicit conversions suffice; no separate equation cards are needed. Questions diagnose bit/byte confusion, average-versus-peak demand and retention. Removed a duplicate sentence left by formula deletion.

One record-storage reference combines rate, size, retention and copies. The visible URL-shortener estimates keep units and limitations explicit. Questions challenge missing copies and hot-set assumptions rather than rehearse multiplication.

No formula card adds to the short metadata/media and ingress/egress comparisons. Numerical examples retain declared exercise assumptions. Questions choose the relevant workload dimensions and challenge automatic database sharding.

One CPU-sizing relationship is useful optional reference. Survivor-first rounding and the 159-server result remain visible with non-CPU caveats. Questions diagnose peaks, placement, overlap in users and replicated work without routine division.

The two-node state trace is the concept and remains visible; no mathematical equation card is needed. Questions distinguish CAP from ACID and follow majority behaviour. Expanded the ambiguous CA label to avoid a certificate-authority dictionary link.

Partition policy is taught through continued operation, conflict resolution and local ATM limits, so no formula is needed. Questions reason about merge semantics and uncoordinated exposure; expanded the ambiguous CA distractor.

PACELC is a decision split rather than an equation. Normal-operation locality and the remote-survival contract remain visible; linearisability is no longer presented as alone requiring distant durable acknowledgement. Questions distinguish ordering, durability and read-your-writes.

One optional card states fixed-set intersection and majority size; visible A/B/C reasoning supports the question with it closed. Quorum overlap is not overstated as linearisability, and ZooKeeper/etcd read-contract differences remain explicit.

Unchanged lesson and question already test an explicit business decision using visible consistency guarantees and a short conditional update. No formula or extra analogy is useful; the SQL predicate effect was independently exercised.

The acknowledgement table and short flush-sharing example carry the concept without equations. Questions trace the promise and failure window; batching feedback now allows measured latency improvements and removes an unsupported zone-latency figure.

The cost scenario keeps its business assumptions and distinguishes allowance from forecast without a formula. Questions check omitted consequences and actual cross-zone bytes; no price recall or arithmetic is needed.

No formula improves the team/complexity and build-versus-buy decisions. Retained questions compare ownership, reversible choices and total cost. SQL queue syntax and product configuration fragments are references, not complete runnable deployments.
